title: Audit evidence lifecycle: WORM vault, residency tags, and query/export API
creator: Priya Patel
description:
Summary:
We need a hardened audit-evidence lifecycle that guarantees tamper-evidence, enforces per-region residency and retention windows, and exposes a query/export API for automated evidence bundles. This ticket scopes the engine that writes admin-action, access, and configuration-change events into a write-once vault, attaches cryptographic seals (HSM/KMS-backed), maintains residency metadata, and provides efficient retrieval and long-term export workflows for legal/compliance teams.

Goals:
- Produce a WORM-backed audit vault that prevents mutation of committed evidence and produces verifiable attestations.
- Ensure each record carries residency metadata (region, residency-policy-id) used for retention enforcement and export scoping.
- Implement a Query & Export API to generate signed evidence bundles (ndjson + manifest + anchors) with automated scheduling and manual triggers.
- Integrate with existing KMS/HSM anchoring (see ENG-701245) and the console reporting pipeline for visibility.

Non-goals:
- Full text-search across archived blobs (we will expose indexed metadata and time-range queries; full-text exports are out-of-scope).
- Cross-region migrations of evidence (handled by legal/ops workflow separately).

Design summary:
- Ingest path: existing audit-producer service posts event to audit-ingest topic; ingest worker validates residency metadata, canonicalizes event schema, writes immutable object to WORM storage (S3 ObjectLock-style or equivalent on-premise store) and records a small index row in region-local index database.
- Anchoring & sealing: after object commit, an async notarization worker computes a compact digest (SHA-256) and requests an HSM signature (via KMS/HSM service integrated in ENG-701245). The signature + timestamp is stored as the attestation for the object and appended to a region ledger used for quick verifications.
- Retention enforcement: retention agent periodically reconciles objects against policy (per residency-policy-id). Objects flagged for deletion are NEVER removed from WORM store unless legal release occurs; instead they move into a sealed 'legal_hold_release' state and become available only to the evidence-export flow which records the legal rationale.
- Query & export API: /v1/compliance/evidence/query supports filters (time-range, residency, actor, action-type, retention-state) and returns index results. /v1/compliance/evidence/export initiates bundle creation: collects objects, produces manifest.json, generates a signed proof bundle (manifest + digests + HSM signatures), archives to escrow bucket, and emits webhook + console notification. Exports support formats: ndjson (events), manifest.json, and optional zipped archive.
- Auditing & observability: ingestion latency, attestation latency, export job success rate, and size/cost of stored evidence are tracked on Console dashboards.

Constraints & trade-offs:
- To limit storage cost we keep a small index in the DB and store full events as compressed blobs. Trade-off: search requires index/metadata completeness; we prioritize common filters used by compliance.
- Strong WORM guarantees on cloud rely on ObjectLock + KMS; for on-prem we will ship a light enforcement shim and coordinate with infra team.
- We avoid synchronous HSM stamping in hot path to keep API latency low; attestation is async but order guarantees are provided by index state transitions.

Testing & rollout plan:
- Unit + integration tests for ingest -> commit -> attest pipeline.
- Chaos test: simulate HSM downtime and verify export bundling still produces partial-attestation bundle with clear 'pending' state.
- Canary rollout in staging for one region (us-west-2) and one test tenant with policy requiring 7 year retention.
- Post-rollout: run an evidence export using /v1/compliance/evidence/export for a 30-day window and run verification against HSM signatures.

Acceptance criteria (see below):
acceptance_criteria: Committed audit objects are immutable: no API or auth path can change or delete a committed object in normal operation.
Every committed object has at least one attestation entry (HSM or queued) and a residency tag (region + residency-policy-id).
Query API supports time-range + residency + actor filters and returns index rows within 2s for common workloads under load test (100 qps).
Export API produces a manifest and signed proof bundle; proof verification must validate HSM signatures recorded in ENG-701245 integration test.
Retention agent prevents accidental deletion and surfaces objects under legal hold state; exports honor legal hold and include required metadata.
Observability dashboards show ingestion latency, attestation success rate, export job status, and storage growth by residency policy.
Security review completed and documented in Confluence; any open findings mitigated or tracked as follow-ups.

2026-03-05 - Priya Patel: Ran cost model with SRE. Expected steady-state monthly storage for 10M events/day is ~2TB compressed across active retention tiers. Added labels for cost-ops follow-up.

2026-03-08 - Thomas Nguyen: Export job prototype created, can produce manifest + bundle; pending HSM integration tests (ENG-701245). Next: add retry/backoff for large exports and console notifications.
notes: Design note: prefer async attestation to preserve ingest P99 under 100ms. Use index state machine to reflect {committed, attested, sealed}.
Edge case: if HSM attestation is delayed >48h, export must include 'signature_pending' flag and exporter must re-run when attestation completes.
Follow-up items: legal-hold UI in Console (separate ticket), cross-region legal-transfer playbook, and long-term escrow automation.
